tasks.short: Take in new purchase prices, set selling prices for over-the-counter stock, get large changes approved, print labels and mark items.

steps.what: Pharmacy technician checks new purchase prices from the wholesaler's price list
Pharmacy technician works out and types selling prices for stock items in the pharmacy system: for every item today, after the change only for items outside the price file and promotions
Pharmacy manager approves price changes above the set percentage
Pharmacy technician checks the final price batch: each changed item, its new selling price against the purchase price, the manager's approvals and running promotions
Pharmacy technician activates the checked price batch in the pharmacy system, so the till and the labels use it
Pharmacy technician selects and prints price labels
Pharmacy technician marks items and shelves with the new labels

tasks.design: The wholesaler's price file is imported into the pharmacy information system ({OTHER}), where the manager's margin and rounding rules set selling prices for over-the-counter stock; only changes above a set percentage go to the manager. The technician prices items outside the file and promotions by hand, checks the final batch and activates it once. Labels for changed items then print in shelf order, and marking the shelves stays manual.
tasks.previous_blocker: Selling prices were worked out item by item from the price list.
tasks.enabler_now: Pharmacy systems import wholesaler price files and apply margin rules.
tasks.still_hard: Some items have no price file entry; promotions need judgement.
tasks.human_edge: Keeping shelves tidy and correctly marked so customers trust the price.
tasks.altitude: The technician reviews exceptions instead of setting each price; pricing rules stay with the manager.

reach.learn: Whether rule-based prices cut till price errors.

evidence.claim: Pharmacy and retail systems import supplier price files and set selling prices by margin rules.
Prices must be shown clearly to consumers under national price indication rules.

assumptions: Boundary: from new purchase prices to marked shelves; prescription medicine prices are outside.
Input contract: price file sent by the wholesaler; margin, rounding and approval threshold set by the pharmacy manager; fallback is typing prices.
Pharmacy manager time is outside the technician's savings.

Marking the shelves, the batch check and the activation keep their full time. s1 keeps 30 for reading the import's exceptions; s2 keeps 10 because items outside the price file and promotions are still priced by hand; s4 keeps 40 because the list of changed items replaces picking them, and printing stays.
research_questions: Do till price errors fall after rule-based pricing?

already_counted.description: Pharmacy technician reviews price exceptions from the import.

incremental.description: Pharmacy manager keeps margin rules current.
No ongoing focal upkeep: pricing items outside the file is kept in s2, and the margin rules are kept by the manager.

approvals.approved_version: The batch of changed items with their new selling prices exactly as checked by the technician in s3b, including the manager's approved changes above the threshold, activated once in the pharmacy system for till and labels; any change needs a new check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: many promotions and items outside the price file, so s1 keeps 50 and s2 keeps 40 (29.7); high: the price file covers most items as designed (40.2).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The pharmacy technician reviews price exceptions and keeps shelves right; price arithmetic disappears.
role.ambitious_version: A technician who never types a price and still never has a wrong one on the shelf.
